Lév. & Vaniot *''Carex ovata'' Merino *''Carex rodriguezii'' Merino | synonyms_ref =   }} '''''Carex binervis''''', the '''green-ribbed sedge''',{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }} is a European species of [[Cyperaceae|sedge]] with an Atlantic distribution. It is found from [[Fennoscandia]] to the [[Iberian Peninsula]], and occurs in [[heath]]s, [[moorland]] and other damp, acidic environments. It typically grows to a height of {{convert|15|-|120|cm|abbr=on|sigfig=1}}, and has [[inflorescence]]s comprising one male and several female [[spike (botany)|spikes]], each up to {{convert|45|mm|abbr=on}} long. The [[utricle (fruit)|utricles]] have two conspicuous green veins, which give rise to both the [[scientific name]] and the [[common name]] of the species. In the vegetative state, it closely resembles ''[[Carex bigelowii|C. bigelowii]]'', a species that usually grows at higher altitude. ''C. binervis'' was first described by [[James Edward Smith (botanist)|James Edward Smith]] in 1800, and is classified in [[Carex sect. Spirostachyae|''Carex'' sect. ''Spirostachyae'']]; several [[hybrid (biology)|hybrids]] with other ''Carex'' species are known. ==Description== ===Vegetative parts=== The [[culm (botany)|culms]] of ''Carex binervis'' are {{convert|15|-|150|cm|ftin|0}} tall, although typically less than {{convert|120|cm|ftin|0|abbr=on}}. They are triangular in section with rounded corners and often a single furrow. The [[leaf|leaves]] are {{convert|7|-|30|cm|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|2|-|6|mm|2}} wide, light green and shiny on the underside, but dark green and matt on the upper surface. The leaves are flat or slightly [[keel]]ed, and taper abruptly to a fine point. The roots of ''C. binervis'' are {{convert|1|-|2|mm|2|abbr=on}} in diameter, with the [[root hair]]s mostly occurring on the short lateral rootlets. The [[rhizome]]s run {{convert|25|-|40|mm|1|abbr=on}} below the soil surface, and are light brown and approximately {{convert|6|mm|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} in diameter. The whole root system reaches a maximum depth of {{convert|18|cm|abbr=on}}, spreading more widely than ''[[Juncus squarrosus]]'', another dominant plant in Atlantic wet heaths.{{cite journal |author1=G. H. Heath |author2=L. C. Luckwill |year=1938 |title=The rooting systems of heath plants |journal=[[Journal of Ecology]] |volume=26 |issue=2 |pages=331–352 |doi=10.2307/2256252 |jstor=2256252 |bibcode=1938JEcol..26..331H }} In the [[:wikt:vegetative|vegetative]] state, ''C. binervis'' is difficult to distinguish from ''[[Carex bigelowii|C. bigelowii]]'', a species that tends to grow at higher altitudes than ''C. binervis''. They differ in that ''C. bigelowii'' has [[glaucous]] leaves and purplish-brown scales on the rhizome, whereas ''C. binervis'' has orange-brown rhizome scales, and leaves which are not glaucous. The leaves of ''C. binervis'' also develop "wine-red" patches on aging, which are never seen in ''C. bigelowii''. ===Reproductive parts=== The [[inflorescence]] of ''C. binervis'' may be up to half the length of the stem. The lower [[bract]]s resemble the leaves, while the upper bracts are more like the [[glume]]s. The inflorescence comprises a single terminal male [[spike (botany)|spike]], and 2–4 lateral female spikes. The male spike is {{convert|20|-|45|mm|1|abbr=on}} long, with purplish glumes which are {{convert|4.0|-|4.5|mm|abbr=on}} long and have a paler midrib. The female spikes are {{convert|15|-|45|mm|1|abbr=on}} long and cylindrical. Their [[Peduncle (botany)|peduncles]] are half sheathed, and up to {{convert|10|cm|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} long, such that the lower female spikes tend to be nodding, while the upper female spikes are erect. The [[utricle (fruit)|utricles]] (seeds) of ''C. binervis'' are {{convert|3.5|-|4.5|mm|abbr=on}} long and broadly elliptical, with a rough, notched beak {{convert|1.0|-|1.5|mm|2|abbr=on}} long. They are purplish brown or sometimes partly green, and both the plant's [[scientific name|scientific]] and [[common name]]s refer to the fact that the utricles are marked with two conspicuous green veins. ''C. binervis'' has a [[chromosome number]] of 2''n'' = 74. ==Distribution and ecology== [[File:Carex binervis habitus.jpg|thumb|''Carex binervis'' in its typical habitat, growing among ''[[Calluna|Calluna vulgaris]]'' (heather)]] ''Carex binervis'' has an oceanic distribution, occurring only in areas of high rainfall, from [[Finland]] and [[Norway]], through the [[British Isles]], [[Germany]], [[Belgium]] and [[France]], to [[Spain]] and [[Portugal]].{{cite web |url=http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?accepted_id=224968&repSynonym_id=-9998&name_id=224968&checklist=monocots |title=''Carex binervis'' |work=World Checklist of Monocotyledons |publisher=[[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew]] |access-date=July 3, 2011}} Within the British Isles, ''Carex binervis'' has a westerly and northerly distribution, and is more abundant in [[Scotland]], [[Wales]] and [[Ireland]] than in [[England]].{{cite web |url=http://www.ukwildflowers.com/Web_pages/carex_binervis_green_ribbed_sedge.htm |title=''Carex binervis'' green-ribbed sedge |author=Peter Llewellyn |work=Wild Flowers of the British Isles |date=March 11, 2010 |access-date=July 3, 2011}} Plants from [[Morocco]] that were previously referred to ''C. binervis'' are now treated as a separate species, ''[[Carex paulo-vargasii|C. paulo-vargasii]]''.{{cite book |author=M. Luceño |year=2008 |title=Cyperaceae – Pontederiaceae |editor1=S. Castroviejo |editor2=M. Luceño |editor3=A. Galán |editor4=P. Jiménez Mejías |editor5=F. Cabezas |editor6=L. Medina |chapter=''Carex'' L. |pages=109–250 |series=[[Flora Iberica]]: Plantas Vasculares de la Península Ibérica e Islas Baleares |volume=18 |publisher=[[Consejo Superior de Investigaciones Científicas]] |isbn=978-84-00-08624-4 |url=http://www.floraiberica.es/floraiberica/texto/pdfs/18_173_20_Carex.pdf }} ''Carex binervis'' grows in acidic, siliceous environments, including "damp [[heath]]s, [[moorland|moors]], rocky places and mountainsides";{{Cite book |author=Clive A. Stace |author-link=Clive A. Stace |year=2010 |title=New Flora of the British Isles |edition=3rd |chapter=''Carex'' L. – sedges |pages=951–974 |publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] |isbn=978-0-521-70772-5}} together with species such as ''[[Deschampsia flexuosa]]'', it is a "useful indicator of acid substrate".{{cite journal|author1=Clare O'Reilly |author2=Chris Metherall |year=2008 |title=County Durham (v.c.66) & South Northumberland (v.c.67) training meeting 7th – 8th July |journal=[[BSBI News]] |volume=108 |page=61 |url=http://www.watsonia.org.uk/BSBINews108.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120321173953/http://www.watsonia.org.uk/BSBINews108.pdf |archive-date=2012-03-21 }} The species has been recorded at altitudes of up to {{convert|930|m}} on [[Glyder Fach]] in north Wales, and there are reports of occurrences up to {{convert|975|m|-2|abbr=on}} in the [[Scottish Highlands]].{{cite web |url=http://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/index.php?q=plant/carex-binervis |title=''Carex binervis'', green-ribbed sedge |work=Online Atlas of the British and Irish Flora |publisher=[[Biological Records Centre]] |access-date=July 3, 2011}} Although sedges are chiefly [[wind pollination|wind pollinated]], insect [[pollinator]]s have been observed to visit ''C. binervis'' occasionally.{{cite journal |author1=Adolfo F. Muñoz Rodríguez |author2=Inmaculada Silva Palacios |author3=Rafael Tormo Molina |year=2007 |title=Cyperaceae and Juncaceae pollination measured in the air at two sites in SW Spain |journal=[[Aerobiologia]] |volume=23 |issue=4 |pages=259–270 |doi=10.1007/s10453-007-9072-0|bibcode=2007Aerob..23..259M |s2cid=189903197 }} ==Taxonomy== In 1800, [[James Edward Smith (botanist)|James Edward Smith]] published an article in the ''[[Transactions of the Linnean Society of London]]'', titled "Descriptions of five new British species of ''Carex''", which included the [[species description|first descriptions]] of ''[[Carex davalliana]]'', ''C. binervis'', ''C. tomentosa'' (a synonym of ''[[Carex filiformis|C. filiformis]]''), ''C. micheliana'' (a synonym of ''[[Carex flacca|C. flacca]]'') and ''[[Carex laevigata|C. laevigata]]''.{{cite journal |author=James Edward Smith |author-link=James Edward Smith (botanist) |year=1800 |title=Descriptions of five new British species of ''Carex'' |journal=[[Transactions of the Linnean Society of London]] |volume=5 |issue=19 |pages=264–273 |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/46568#page/312/mode/1up |doi=10.1111/j.1096-3642.1800.tb00600.x}} After the Latin diagnosis of ''Carex binervis'', Smith writes:
This species appears to have been confounded with ''[[Carex distans|C. distans]]''; and from [[John Lightfoot (biologist)|Lightfoot's]] description of the green angles of the fruit, I presume it to have been what he intended under that name. It is considerably larger than the real ''distans'', the spikes black intermixed with green rather than yellowish, and the female ones often branched or compounded at their base. Its most essential and decisive character however consists in the two strong deep-green nerves or ribs which run along each side of the fruit externally near the edge. The arillus is also broader and more compressed than in ''C. distans''.
''Carex binervis'' is classified in ''Carex'' subsection ''Elatae'', part of [[Carex sect. Spirostachyae|''Carex'' section ''Spirostachyae'']], alongside ''C. laevigata'' and other species.{{cite journal |author1=Marcial Escudero |author2=Modesto Luceño |year=2009 |title=Systematics and evolution of ''Carex'' sects. ''Spirostachyae'' and ''Elatae'' (Cyperaceae) |journal=[[Plant Systematics and Evolution]] |volume=279 |issue=1–4 |pages=163–189 |doi=10.1007/s00606-009-0156-x|bibcode=2009PSyEv.279..163E |s2cid=29472803 }} Natural [[hybrid (biology)|hybrids]] are known between ''C. binervis'' and various other ''Carex'' species, including ''C. laevigata'' (forming ''C. × deserta''), ''[[Carex viridula|C. viridula]]'' (forming ''C. × corstorphinei''), ''[[Carex punctata|C. punctata]]'' and ''[[Carex flava|C. flava]]''.{{cite book |author1=A. C. Jermy |author2=D. A. Simpson |author3=M. J. Y. Foley |author4=M. S. Porter |year=2007 |title=Sedges of the British Isles |edition=3rd |series=BSBI Handbook No. 1 |isbn=978-0-901158-35-2 |publisher=[[Botanical Society of the British Isles]] |chapter=''Carex binervis'' Sm. |pages=358–360}} ==References== {{Reflist|32em}} ==External links== *{{Commons category-inline|Carex binervis|''Carex binervis''}} *[https://web.archive.org/web/20131030094754/http://www.plant-identification.co.uk/skye/cyperaceae/carex-binervis.htm ''Carex binervis''], West Highland Flora {{Good article}} {{Taxonbar|from=Q160245}} [[Category:Carex|binervis]] [[Category:Flora of Europe]] [[Category:Plants described in 1800]]
